title: Nebraska, Matt Rhule enjoy reprieve with rout at Rutgers in rare November win
content:
Nebraska’s losing streak is over. The Huskers got a November victory, just the third in 14 tries under coach Matt Rhule, after beating Rutgers 31-0 on Saturday at SHI Stadium to achieve bowl eligibility for the third straight season.

Nebraska’s first win in 42 days came with some of the clumsiness and frustration that marred the previous four games, all Big Ten losses. But the Huskers leaned on the ground game, rushing for 237 yards on 43 carries under the direction of newly promoted offensive coordinator Glenn Thomas.

Freshman running back Jamal Rule ran for 103 yards on a career-high 22 carries. QB Anthony Colandrea spread the football between his backs and tight ends. The Huskers manufactured scoring drives of 94 and 90 yards in the first half, mixing 20 runs with six passes.

“That’s who we are,” Rhule said. “That’s who we want to be.”

And finally, they can take a deep breath. The shutout was Nebraska’s first in conference play since beating Iowa State 28-0 in 2003. Rutgers managed just 143 yards and 42 yards passing, both Big Ten-era bests for the Huskers on defense.

As losses mounted in October and into this month, disappointment among the passionate Nebraska fanbase reached a peak not seen in years. Rhule, 25-23 at Nebraska in four seasons, fired OC Dana Holgorsen last week after a 24-13 loss at Illinois.

Rhule extended the contract of defensive coordinator Rob Aurich. It didn’t stop the critics. And a victory over Rutgers (2-8, 1-6 Big Ten), already at the bottom of the Big Ten and hobbled Saturday at quarterback and wide receiver, won’t silence the doubters.

But Nebraska (6-4, 3-4) clings to hope of a productive season with Ohio State visiting Lincoln next Saturday and a trip to Iowa on Black Friday after that.

“Hopefully people back home are happy with the result,” Rhule said. “I know the guys were.”

Here are our takeaways:

In the four defeats since Oct. 10, Nebraska led entering the fourth quarter against Indiana, Oregon and Washington. It outgained its opponents in three of the losses and equaled the Ducks in yardage.

But the Huskers featured nothing in particular on offense. They passed the ball on 55 percent of their offensive snaps. On fourth-and-1 last week at Illinois? An incompletion.

Maybe that was the breaking point. Because Nebraska, with Rhule in the ear of Thomas, was not going to go down Saturday without running the football. And running it again. Thomas called run plays on the first seven offensive snaps.

They came out to make a statement.

At the end, the run-pass split was 43-25.

“This is what I want the football team to look like,” Rhule said. “We’re going to run the ball.”

Rhule said he was more involved in the offensive plan during the week and the play calling Saturday. His voice on the headset, in fact, contributed to problems early with Nebraska’s helmet communications, according to Colandrea.

Nevertheless, Nebraska got what it wanted.

“This is good for our guys,” Colandrea said.

The run-heavy plan allowed Colandrea to flourish in play action. Notably, he shrugged off his wide receivers, who did not catch a pass in the first half as Nebraska built a 14-0 lead. Tight ends and running backs finished with 11 of the Huskers’ 16 catches.

Colandrea finished 15-of-22 passing for 188 yards and touchdown throws to tight ends Luke Lindenmeyer and Carter Nelson. The QB also rushed for 66 yards and one score.

Nebraska led the Big Ten entering Saturday with 8.3 penalties per game for an average of 70.8 yards. Saturday’s performance started on a rocky note with three pre-snap flags on the Huskers’ first two possessions.

The second drive went up in flames because of a false start on left guard Gibson Pyle and an illegal shift on wide receiver Jacory Barney Jr.

Rhule called a timeout before a third-and-14 play on the same possession. Out of the stoppage, the routes of receivers Quinn Clark and Kwazi Gilmer converged as Colandrea’s throw fell incomplete.

From there, the play got cleaner. Nebraska identified a Rutgers vulnerability on a third-quarter punt. The Huskers checked into a fake. It was there, but Nelson’s throw to Jeremiah Charles fell short.

“The most important thing for me today: It wasn’t perfect, but it was certainly a step in the right direction,” Rhule said.

Nebraska finished with six penalties for 50 yards.

Work remains. The Huskers must play sharper than they did Saturday to beat Ohio State or Iowa. But a convincing win in November represents progress. Opportunity awaits.

The Huskers said they’re hungry to prove something beyond Saturday.

“Our record right now isn’t showing who we are,” safety Jamir Conn said. “We’re one of the best teams in the nation. And these next couple games, we’re going to put it out there.”

Rutgers dealt with a difficult situation Saturday, playing without top quarterback Dylan Lonergan. With three-game starter AJ Surace hurt last week against Wisconsin, the Scarlet Knights started Sean Ashenfelder.

He was hurt on Rutgers’ third possession when sacked by Jahsear Whittington. Surace replaced Ashenfelder. And Nebraska took advantage, intercepting Surace twice. Caleb Benning and Jeremiah Charles notched picks in the second half.

Despite the shutout, not all went well for the Huskers defensively. Whittington, a top defensive lineman, was hurt in the second half while recording a tackle for loss on a running play. He limped off the field with an apparent lower-body injury.

Nebraska was already without defensive end Anthony Jones, linebacker Owen Chambliss and cornerback Andrew Marshall. Left guard Paul Mubenga also left the game in the first half.
